turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
You need an answer from me? I'm the one who walked in here without one. You entered that zero before you spoke to Owen or to me, so tell me what you're holding besides a machine's guess.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

"Admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript" — I'm writing that down word for word. Owen has nothing to admit, and your own procedure, 4.4, says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment with nothing on his record, not an ultimatum. Show me a document, or I walk straight to the principal's office from here.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

"The only two options." Your school's procedure lists a third one, Hale, and you skipped steps 4.1 and 4.2 to get here. I'm not picking anything; I'm going upstairs to the principal unless you put a document in front of me now.
